correctness.rationale: For chi<1 the four-state generator is irreducible; conditional second moments solve a linear Markov-modulated OU system (2diag(2k+phi)-M)g=D_x 1. Perron-Frobenius positivity for the shifted Metzler generator ensures finiteness iff its spectral bound is negative; exact determinant and principal-block analysis give the stated D(delta)>0 threshold, with positive stationary stochastic convolution even if its variance diverges. A fresh independent SymPy construction of the entire generator verified det=64(2k+lambda)D(delta), the inverse conditioned moment h=g_2=g_4, Mpsi=-2lambda psi, diag(2k+phi)psi=2k psi and the derivative d h/d delta =D_x lambda c²[k(2k+lambda)-2c²]/[4D(delta)^2]. This backward eigenmode yields the velocity covariance e^{-2(k+lambda)t}; integrating Green–Kubo gives the full MSD and long-time diffusion. A stable k=1,lambda=2,c=3/2 example has critical delta=1/7. The finite symbolic/numerical checks corroborate these identities; irreducibility and positivity arguments justify parameter-wide statements.

value.rationale: This resolves a physically motivated parameter interpolation omitted in the primary model. Sharp second-moment divergence, asynchrony-driven stabilization, sign-reversing effect on diffusivity, and fixed velocity-memory rate separate fluctuation amplitude from persistence. Such a complete transport phase diagram is more than a routine positivity calculation or marginal parameter perturbation.

final_claim: For the four-state correlated telegraph nonreciprocal Brownian dimer with stiffness k>0, switching rate lambda>0, amplitude c>=0, bare diffusion D_x>0 and partial synchrony chi in [0,1), delta=1-chi, a stationary path law exists under positive average damping and has finite second moment exactly when D(delta)=k(k+lambda*delta)(2k+lambda)-c²(2k+lambda*delta)>0. Then the active-velocity covariance is an exact positive exponential e^{-2(k+lambda)t}, and the center-of-mass MSD and D_eff are given by the closed h formula h=D_x[(k+lambda*delta)(2k+lambda)-2c²]/[4D(delta)] and E[X_t-X_0]^2=D_x t+[2c²h/(k+lambda)]t-[c²h/(k+lambda)²](1-e^{-2(k+lambda)t}), D_eff=D_x/2+c²h/(k+lambda). The derivative wrt delta changes sign at c²=k(2k+lambda)/2, independently of the finite-second-moment stability boundary. No claims of higher stationary moments or irreducibility at chi=1.
limitations: Chi in [0,1), positive stiffness and switching rate, four-state telegraph process without nonlinear steric forces.
Stationary path existence is distinct from finite stationary second moments; non-finiteness is not non-existence.
No higher-moment or tail law or independent noise correlation beyond the specified switching generator.
